claim: This test is a test used in diagnosing the disease "diphtheria".
context: diagnosis: Culture and toxigenicity testing — Diagnosis is clinical and is confirmed by isolating a member of the C. diphtheriae species complex and then demonstrating toxin production. Species identification alone is insufficient, because tox-bearing isolates may still fail to express toxin: in the French Guiana series five isolates were tox-positive by PCR yet all were negative by Elek test. Phenotypic toxigenicity testing therefore governs whether antitoxin is indicated.

context: diagnosis: Audiometric and pedigree diagnosis — Clinical assessment in the original pedigree combined otoscopy, pure-tone air- and bone-conduction audiometry, oto-immittance, DPOAE and pedigree analysis. History and examination assessed acquired causes and syndromic features. DFNA53 attribution requires evidence connecting the family to the mapped locus; a similar audiogram or a negative gene panel alone does not establish this diagnosis. This row names several distinct assessments; the measurements below are LOINC-coded for the pure-tone air-conduction audiometric component only, matching the exact seven frequencies the founding report tested, not for bone-conduction audiometry, otoscopy, oto-immittance or DPOAE also described here.
